- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior 30d mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior 7d high), model often overshoots in next 7–14d; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak (e.g., 3+ days of 0.00), model may lag in catching the rebound; adjust forecast to align with 3–5d moving average of true prices.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) for 5+ consecutive days, model tends to underestimate; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion toward prior 14d average.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome deviates >3% from 30d moving average of history, adjust forecast to align with 30d SMA, especially if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- If sentiment is positive but model forecast is below 70% of 30d SMA, consider a 1–2% upward bias to reflect sentiment-driven momentum.
